label: V2
prompt:
You maintain the long-term memory of a wellness and physical-therapy chat assistant. You read part of a conversation and decide which durable facts about the USER must be written down, changed or removed. Your answer is read by a program, not by a person, so reply with a single JSON object and nothing else.

You are given:
- the date of the conversation;
- the facts already stored for this user. Each has an "id", the fact text, a "category" and a "locked" flag. Locked means the user typed that fact in themselves;
- the messages to read, each labelled [user] or [assistant]. The input says whether they are a whole conversation or a single turn (one user message and the assistant's reply to it). In the single-turn case the stored facts already include what earlier turns produced.

OUTPUT FORMAT
{"operations": [ ... ]}
Each operation is exactly one of:
{"op": "ADD", "fact": "<text>", "category": "<category>"}
{"op": "UPDATE", "id": "<id of a stored fact>", "fact": "<new full text>", "category": "<category>"}
{"op": "DELETE", "id": "<id of a stored fact>"}
An empty list, {"operations": []}, means "nothing new". It is the normal answer for most conversations. Never write an operation just to have one.

WHAT MAY BE WRITTEN DOWN
- Only what the USER said about themselves. Never something the assistant suggested, assumed or guessed, even if the user did not object. Never your own inference. Never something about another person: a relative's or friend's condition is not a fact about the user.
- Durable facts only: still true and useful a month from now, in a conversation about something else. Not passing states (tired today, a bad night), not the details of a one-off request (the routine they asked for today, an event tomorrow), not small talk.
- Health facts are wanted: injuries, surgeries, diagnoses the user reports, ongoing pain, movements a clinician told them to avoid. Also goals; lasting personal likes, dislikes and habits, the things a friend would remember about them (a favourite food or drink, a sport or hobby, how they like to be spoken to, how answers should be written); and basic profile facts (job, routine, equipment). A lasting like or habit counts even when it is mentioned in passing; what happened today does not.
- Never store identifiers: ID or card numbers, phone numbers, e-mail addresses, street addresses. If the user gives one, leave it out entirely.
- Resolve relative times with the conversation date. "Three months ago", "last month", "since last winter", "recently" must become an absolute month and year (for example "July 2026"), because a relative time is wrong a month later. If it cannot be made absolute, leave the time out rather than keep a relative one.

CATEGORIES (closed list, use exactly these words)
- condition: injuries, surgeries, diagnoses, ongoing pain or symptoms
- restriction: movements, loads or activities the user must or wants to avoid
- goal: something the user is working towards
- preference: lasting likes, dislikes, and how they want answers written
- profile: other stable facts about the user (job, routine, equipment, schedule)

HOW TO COMPARE WITH STORED FACTS
- The same fact is already stored: do nothing.
- The user's new statement changes or extends a stored fact: UPDATE it, using the stored id. Write the complete new text. When the old state matters, keep it briefly, for example "now pain-free when walking (in July 2026: pain after 10 minutes)".
- The user says a stored fact is no longer true: DELETE it, using the stored id.
- A locked fact must never be updated or deleted. If the user contradicts a locked fact, ADD the user's new statement as a new fact instead.
- Only use ids that appear in the stored facts. Never invent an id.
- Do not repeat in an ADD a fact that is already stored.

STYLE OF EACH FACT
- At most 5 operations in total, and each fact at most 300 characters.
- One fact per operation. Several facts mean several operations.
- Write each fact in the language the user wrote it in, as a short neutral statement about the user, understandable without the conversation (no "she said", no "as above").
- Only what was said. Do not add details, causes, severity or advice.

EXAMPLES (structure only; write facts in the user's own language)
User says they had a meniscus operation in May 2025 and nothing is stored:
{"operations": [{"op": "ADD", "fact": "Had meniscus surgery in May 2025", "category": "condition"}]}
User says "my back is fine now" and stored fact f2 says "Has lower back pain":
{"operations": [{"op": "DELETE", "id": "f2"}]}
User only chats, asks for a one-off routine, or the assistant guesses a diagnosis the user never confirmed:
{"operations": []}

messages.content: Chào bạn. Mình bị đau lưng dưới khoảng 2 năm nay, bác sĩ bảo là thoát vị đĩa đệm L4-L5.

Chào bạn, cảm ơn bạn đã chia sẻ. Đau lưng dưới kéo dài như vậy chắc hẳn rất khó chịu. Mình có thể gợi ý một số bài vận động nhẹ nhàng, nhưng bạn nên trao đổi thêm với bác sĩ điều trị trước khi tăng cường độ nhé.
Vậy mình nên tập gì buổi sáng cho đỡ cứng lưng?
Bạn có thể thử bài xoay nhẹ hông khi nằm ngửa và bài mèo-bò trên bốn điểm chống. Mỗi bài làm chậm 8-10 lần, dừng ngay nếu thấy đau lan xuống chân. Tránh cúi gập người về phía trước khi mới ngủ dậy.

messages.content: I had ACL reconstruction on my right knee in March 2025.
Thanks for telling me. That's a big recovery, and a year and a half out you're probably well into strengthening. How is the knee feeling day to day?
Mostly fine. What can I do to strengthen it further?

Good options are step-ups, single-leg glute bridges and slow tempo squats within a comfortable range. Aim for two or three sessions a week and stop if you feel sharp pain or the knee feels unstable. Your surgeon or physio can tell you which load level is right for you.

messages.content: Hôm nay trời đẹp ghê, mình vừa đi chợ về xong. À mà mình bị tiểu đường type 2 nên phải kiêng đồ ngọt lắm. Bạn gợi ý giúp mình bài tập nhẹ buổi sáng được không?

Nghe thích quá, đi chợ sáng sớm là một cách vận động rất tốt đó. Với buổi sáng, bạn có thể đi bộ nhanh 15-20 phút rồi giãn cơ nhẹ nhàng. Nếu bạn đang dùng thuốc hạ đường huyết, hãy ăn nhẹ trước khi tập và mang theo ít đường phòng khi cần.
Cảm ơn bạn, mình sẽ thử.
Chúc bạn có buổi sáng thật vui. Nếu thấy chóng mặt hay run tay khi tập thì nghỉ ngay và đo lại đường huyết nhé.

messages.content: Ha, my cat knocked my coffee over again this morning. Anyway, I've had a rotator cuff tear in my left shoulder for a while now so anything overhead is out. Can you suggest an upper body workout?

Cats and coffee, a classic. For an upper body session that keeps your hands below shoulder height, you could do rows with a band, bicep curls and wall push-ups. Keep the range comfortable and stop if the shoulder pinches.
Nice, the band rows sound good.
Great. Start with two sets of twelve with a light band and slow control on the way back. Let me know if you'd like a progression for next week.

messages.content: Mình hay ngồi máy tính nhiều, cổ cứng lắm. Có bài nào giãn cổ không?

Với tình trạng cổ cứng kéo dài, nhiều khả năng bạn đang bị thoái hóa đốt sống cổ hoặc thoát vị đĩa đệm cổ. Bạn nên đi chụp MRI để chắc chắn. Trong lúc đó, bạn có thể nghiêng đầu sang hai bên, giữ 15 giây mỗi bên, lặp lại 3 lần.
Ừ, cho mình thêm vài bài giãn cơ đơn giản nữa đi.
Bạn thử thêm bài xoay vai ra sau 10 lần và bài đặt tay lên đầu, kéo nhẹ đầu về một bên. Làm chậm và đều hơi thở, đừng giật mạnh.

messages.content: Can you give me a 10 minute morning routine?

Sure. Since you probably have tight hips from sitting and maybe some mild sciatica, I'd start with gentle hip openers, then a few cat-cows and finish with a standing forward fold. Take each move slowly and breathe.
Sounds good, thanks.
You're welcome. Let me know if you'd like a shorter evening version as well.

messages.content: Đầu gối mình khỏi hẳn rồi, không còn đau nữa.
Tin vui quá! Nghe vậy là phần hồi phục của bạn đang đi đúng hướng. Bạn vẫn nên tăng lại cường độ từ từ để khớp quen dần.
Vậy mình tập squat lại được chưa?
Bạn có thể bắt đầu với squat chạm ghế, 2 hiệp 10 lần, rồi tăng dần sau mỗi tuần. Nếu có cảm giác nhói ở gối thì dừng lại và giảm biên độ.

messages.content: Good news, my doctor cleared me to run again. The shin splints are completely gone.
That's great to hear! Since you've been off running for a while, build back gradually. A run-walk interval format works well for the first couple of weeks.
What would a first week look like?

Try three sessions: one minute easy jog, two minutes walk, repeated eight times. Keep every session on soft ground if you can and leave a rest day between them. If the shin ache comes back, drop back a step.

messages.content: Giờ mình đi bộ cả tiếng cũng không đau gối nữa, nhưng leo cầu thang vẫn còn hơi nhói.
Tiến bộ rõ rệt đó! Đi bộ cả tiếng mà không đau là dấu hiệu tốt. Leo cầu thang đòi hỏi gối chịu lực nhiều hơn nên nhói nhẹ cũng là chuyện dễ hiểu ở giai đoạn này.
Mình nên tập gì để leo cầu thang đỡ nhói?
Bài bước lên bậc thấp (step-up) rất hợp, bắt đầu với bậc cao 10-15 cm, 2 hiệp 8 lần mỗi chân. Giữ đầu gối thẳng hàng với ngón chân và bước xuống thật chậm.

messages.content: Quick update: I started seeing a physio and now the pain only comes when I lift heavy things. Sitting is fine.
That's a nice change. Pain that only shows up under load usually points to what to train rather than what to avoid. Your physio will be the best guide on how heavy to go.
Any tips for lifting groceries without it flaring up?
Hinge at the hips instead of rounding your back, keep the bags close to your body and split the load between both hands. Two lighter trips are better than one heavy one while it settles.

messages.content: Mình mới bị bong gân mắt cá chân trái tuần trước, giờ đi lại vẫn còn sưng.
Mình rất tiếc khi nghe vậy. Bong gân còn sưng thì bạn nên cho chân nghỉ, kê cao khi ngồi và chườm lạnh. Nếu sưng không giảm sau vài ngày hoặc không chịu lực được thì nên đi khám nhé.

messages.content: Hey, I'm back. I broke my wrist skiing last month and the cast just came off.
Welcome back, and glad the cast is off. The wrist will be stiff and the forearm muscles weaker for a while. Did your doctor or physio give you any guidance?
Yes, my physio told me to avoid push-ups and any weight-bearing on that hand for another six weeks.
That's a sensible restriction. In the meantime we can work on gentle range of motion: wrist circles, finger flexes and tendon glides, all without load.
Cool. My goal is to be back on skis by February, so I want to be strong by then.
February is realistic if healing goes to plan. We can build a progression: mobility now, light grip work after your physio approves, then loaded wrist and shoulder strength closer to the season.
Sounds like a plan. Show me today's mobility routine.
Do wrist circles ten times each direction, then ten slow finger flexes and extensions, and finish with five tendon glides. Repeat the set twice and stop if it hurts.

messages.content: ugh, today was a mess. I had pizza for lunch and then went for a long walk by the river
A long walk by the river sounds like a good way to balance the pizza. How are your legs feeling after it?
fine, a bit tired. I also watched two movies in the evening, lazy day
Lazy days are allowed. Tomorrow we can ease back in with something short if you feel like it.
chị gái mình mê chạy bộ lắm, tuần nào cũng chạy ba buổi, còn nhà mình thì mẹ thích nấu ăn
Chị bạn chăm thật đấy, còn mẹ nấu ăn ngon thì cả nhà có phúc rồi. Bạn thì sao, hôm nay muốn nói chuyện gì?
mình chưa nghĩ ra, chắc hỏi bạn về giấc ngủ
Được chứ. Bạn thường đi ngủ lúc mấy giờ và có hay thức giữa đêm không?
what should I do this weekend to stay active
You probably like hiking, a lot of people who ask this do. A trail walk on Saturday could be a nice option. What kind of outdoor stuff do you usually enjoy?
haha who knows, I'll see how the weather is
Fair enough. If the weather is bad, a short indoor session works too.
